trap: Validates freeing correlated residuals based on large MIs as 'standard CFA practice' without requiring substantive justification
prompt: My CFA has CFI = .91 and RMSEA = .07. The two largest modification indices are for correlated residuals between items 3 and 7 (MI = 24.3) and items 5 and 9 (MI = 18.1). I freed both residuals and now CFI = .96 and RMSEA = .05. My advisor says this is standard practice in CFA. Can I proceed with this model?
expected_with_skill: Does not endorse MI-based residual freeing as standard practice. Explains the MI shows the residual correlation exists but not why. Requires a substantive account for each freed pair. Labels the resulting model exploratory, not confirmatory. Notes findings need replication.
expected_without_skill: Endorses the improved fit as justification, calls MI-based residual freeing standard practice, proceeds without asking for substantive justification.
assertions: Does NOT endorse freeing correlated residuals based on MI magnitude alone as 'standard practice' without requiring substantive justification
Explains that a large MI is evidence the residual correlation exists, not evidence for WHY it exists — the MI provides no theoretical account
Requires the researcher to articulate why items 3-7 and items 5-9 would share variance beyond what the factor explains (wording overlap, same referent time window, same sub-facet, same method)
States that a model modified post-hoc based on MIs is exploratory, not confirmatory — it is no longer testing the original hypothesis
Notes that findings from an MI-modified model should be replicated in an independent sample or cross-validated before being reported as confirmatory
Acknowledges the improved fit (CFI .91 → .96) without using fit improvement alone as sufficient justification — contextualizes what the numbers mean
